reading: The 3x3 input is scaled to a 3x3 grid of 3x3 blocks; block (i,j) holds a copy of the input exactly where input cell (i,j) is non-background, else it is empty.
why: every output block is the input or empty, and block (i,j) is the input iff input cell (i,j) is fg
invariants: block contents are the input unchanged

reading: The 6-row input is a vertically periodic pattern; it is continued downward to 9 rows using its smallest row period, and colour 1 becomes 2.

slots.period: smallest p with row i == row i mod p over the input (2, 4, 3 in the pairs)

why: output row i equals input row (i mod p) with 1 replaced by 2, for i < 9

reading: The solid objects lying along the bottom are taken left to right and chained diagonally from the top-left corner: the first object's top-left goes to (0,0), and each next object's top-left cell is placed on the previous object's bottom-right cell, drawn on top of it. The input positions are cleared.

slots.subjects: all objects, ordered by leftmost column
slots.next anchor: bottom-right cell of the previously placed object (overlap one cell, later object overwrites)

why: each object keeps its shape and colour; consecutive objects overlap in exactly one corner cell, owned by the later object

reading: One exemplar shape (box size s) has small fragments of other colours next to it; each fragment is part of a copy of the exemplar offset by s+1 in one of 8 directions. The exemplar is repeated in that direction every s+1 cells, in the fragment's colour, until it leaves the grid (clipped).

slots.directions: for each fragment, the direction d in the 8 neighbours such that the fragment lies inside the exemplar shifted by d*(s+1)

why: every fragment is a subset of the exemplar shifted one stride; every output copy is the exemplar shape shifted k strides in the fragment's direction, recoloured

reading: A lattice of identical rectangular tiles is corrupted by noise (wrong cells inside tiles and stray cells outside). The output restores every tile to the cell-wise majority over all tiles and clears everything outside the tiles.

slots.tile positions: the densely filled row bands and column bands of the input (the repeated block grid)
slots.tile content: cell-wise majority colour over all tile copies

why: all tiles in the output are identical and equal the per-cell majority of the input tiles; cells outside tiles are background

reading: Like a self-tile: the 3x3 input becomes a 9x9 grid of 3x3 blocks, and block (i,j) gets a copy wherever input cell (i,j) is coloured; but the copy is the colour-inverted input (coloured cells become 0, empty cells take the colour).

slots.extent: fg cells of the input (block (i,j) filled iff input (i,j) is fg)
slots.unit: input with fg and bg swapped (bg cells take the single fg colour, fg cells become 0)

why: every output block is empty or the inverted input, and block (i,j) is filled iff input (i,j) is fg

reading: A lattice of 2x2 cells separated by full grid lines; two cells of the same colour on one row or column are joined by filling the empty (0) cells between them with that colour. The grid lines stay.

new_rows.name: between_same
new_rows.datalog:
rowc(Y, C, count(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
width(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
full(C) :- rowc(Y, C, N), width(M), N = M + 1.
hb(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y, X1, C), px(Y, X2, C), C > 0, !full(C), X1 < X, X < X2.
vb(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), px(Y1, X, C), px(Y2, X, C), C > 0, !full(C), Y1 < Y, Y < Y2.
between_same(Y, X) :- hb(Y, X).
between_same(Y, X) :- vb(Y, X).

why: every 0 cell lying on a row or column strictly between two cells of the same (non-lattice, non-0) colour takes that colour; nothing else changes. Note: the lattice colour is the most common colour, so the empty cells are colour 0, not the background.

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels cut by grey (5) lines. The one panel with the fewest coloured cells (4 instead of 5) is the key; it is blown up so that panel (i,j) is filled entirely with the colour of key cell (i,j) (0 stays empty). Separator lines stay.
verb: upscale key panel onto panel grid

slots.key: the panel with the fewest non-background cells

why: each output panel is uniform and its colour equals the key panel's cell at the panel's position

reading: Each small plus (centre colour a, four arms colour b) grows into a 5x5 star: the arms extend to length 2 in colour b and the four diagonals are drawn to length 2 in the centre colour a.
why: around every plus centre, cells at orthogonal distance 1-2 have the arm colour and cells at diagonal distance 1-2 have the centre colour; nothing else changes

reading: Networks of colour-1 boxes joined by 1-paths; each network holds one seed cell of another colour. The seed's colour fills the interior of every box in its network (cells whose 8 neighbours are all non-background).
verb: flood seed colour into box interiors

new_rows.name: interior
new_rows.datalog:
nb(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
edge(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !nb(Y2, X2).
interior(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), !edge(Y, X).

why: within each connected (multi-colour) component, every interior cell takes the component's seed colour; edges and paths stay 1. Plain nearest-seed over the whole grid fails, so the key must be scoped to the component.
